messages.subject: propto calcs for lkj_cov?
parts:
I'm updating the LKJ functions to ensure their
types are OK with mixed arguments. So far, I've
only needed to change a couple types assigned to
double that should've had template params.

But I'm wondering if I can drop some of the calcs
under propto=true conditions.

For instance, in lkj_cov.hpp, if neither eta nor y are parameters,
then all the increments to lp after the if (eta == 1.0) test can
be dropped, including the ones inside the test body and after.

Assuming lkj_corr_log did the right thing w.r.t. propto,
what would wind up happening is a bunch of extra work to
add 0 to lp, which just adds extra tests and function calls.
It won't actually add 0 to lp when doing lp += 0, because
there's a test on += for this case to avoid over-allocation of
autodif vars.

- Bob

parts:
Did we get the theory squared away on the phone?

In commit 41418d856ec792c5220ea944c72e9c3742b14344, you commented

src/stan/prob/distributions/multivariate/continuous/lkj_cov.hpp:69: D.diagonal() = sds.inverse();  // FIXME:  D.diagonal() inefficient

How is this inefficient? If D is an Eigen::DiagonalMatrix, then the off-diagonals are not allocated and Eigen has specializations for multiplying it by something. Are you saying that Stan is inefficient because it promotes D to a full matrix before multiplying?

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: propto calcs for lkj_cov?
parts:
On 9/10/12 9:34 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> Did we get the theory squared away on the phone?

Yes. The patches are all checked in in case you
want to check them out.

We also made sure all the calls did the right
thing with respect to propagating error policies.

We still need error checks that the the matrices
passed in are square, but I think we need them
everywhere along with range checks on all of our
matrix ops. And we could stand to generalize
check_finite to matrices.

I'm also still not sure about the decision to check
finiteness of parameters not variates. It's what
Boost did, but it made sense there because you'd
construct a normal(mu,sigma) and then pass multiple y
to it.

I just realized there's a mismatch
because there's no test in the second lkj_cov_log
function.

All of this error checking could stand to be reviewed
along with all the rest of our code :-)

> In commit 41418d856ec792c5220ea944c72e9c3742b14344, you commented
>
> src/stan/prob/distributions/multivariate/continuous/lkj_cov.hpp:69: D.diagonal() = sds.inverse(); // FIXME:
> D.diagonal() inefficient
>
> How is this inefficient? If D is an Eigen::DiagonalMatrix, then the off-diagonals are not allocated and Eigen has
> specializations for multiplying it by something. Are you saying that Stan is inefficient because it promotes D to a full
> matrix before multiplying?

I commented too soon and never reviewed later.

Here's the code:

Eigen::DiagonalMatrix<T_y,Eigen::Dynamic> D(K);
D.diagonal() = sds.inverse();
lp += lkj_corr_log<propto,T_y,T_shape,Policy>(D * y * D, eta, Policy());

Because D and y share the same underlying scalar type (T_y),
I didn't have to convert the expression from
D * y * D to multiply(D,multiply(y,D)) as I was imagining
when I wrote the comment; the latter would've caused
not one, but two promotions from diagonal to full matrix.
I also suspect lkj_corr_log would have an issue, but it won't
because D * y * D is already a full matrix.

I just pushed a patch to remove the offending comment :-)
Thanks for reminding me.

- Bob
